newsitem.title: USA: US rail freight traffic up sharply from yr ago-AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail freight traffic up sharply from yr ago-AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight carloads, ton-miles and intermodal rose sharply in the week ended February 1 from the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said carloads in the week totaled 335,317, up 11.2 percent from 301,537 in the year-ago week. Ton-miles rose 11.9 percent to 26.4 billion from 23.6 billion a year ago. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
AAR said intermodal volume, which does not include carloads, increased 7.1 percent in the week to 163,147 trailers and containers from 152,346 a year ago.

"Especially encouraging is the overall health of the national economy -- steady growth, vigorous industrial production, moderate interest rates, active exports and sustained housing activity," Craig Rockey, AAR senior assistant vice president, said.

"The year is obviously young, but the level and relative consistency of the weekly figures coupled with the favorable economic environment augurs well for a continuation of early favorable trends," Rockey added.
AAR said carloads of metallic ores rose 17.3 percent to 14,358 from 12,236 a year ago, while grain loadings were up 13.1 percent to 26,244 from 23,212 last year.

Coal carloads also increased 16.5 percent to 130,465 from 111,963 in the same 1996 week, while petroleum loadings grew 8.3 percent to 5,519 carloads from 5,096. Motor vehicles and equipment carloads totaled 21,373, up 9.7 percent from 19,484 last year.
But nonmetallic minerals loadings fell 11 percent in the week to 8,044 carloads from 9,040 last year, while farm products other than grain dipped 3.7 percent to 1,284 carloads from 1,333.
In the first five weeks of 1997, AAR said that ton-miles rose 5.5 percent from the same 1996 period. Carloads were up 4.4 percent and intermodal freight rose 3.9 percent, it said.

In a separate accounting, AAR said U.S. intermodal traffic to Canada in the February 1 week totaled 26,214 trailers and containers, up 21 percent from the year-ago week. It said U.S. carloads to Canada were 48,132, up two percent from a year ago.
